codes.name: Belonging
codes.definition: The participant describes feeling accepted, included or part of a community (class, program, peer group, field).
codes.include_when: Explicit statements about fitting in, being welcomed, having 'my people', or feeling like a real member.
codes.exclude_when: Mere mentions of other people without any sense of inclusion or exclusion. Use 'Isolation' for the absence of belonging.

examples.quote: For the first time I felt like I was actually one of them, not just a visitor.
The study group became my people.

codes.name: Isolation
codes.definition: The participant describes feeling alone, excluded, invisible or disconnected from others in the learning setting.
codes.include_when: Being left out, not knowing anyone, having no one to ask, feeling like an outsider.
codes.exclude_when: Choosing to work alone without any negative feeling.

examples.quote: I'd sit in the back and nobody would talk to me for the whole quarter.
I prefer doing problem sets alone, it's faster.
examples.note: Working alone by choice is not isolation.

codes.name: Help-seeking
codes.definition: The participant describes asking for, or deciding not to ask for, academic or personal help (from instructors, peers, tutors, services or AI tools).
codes.include_when: Office hours, tutoring, asking classmates, emailing a professor, using a chatbot to get unstuck, and also explicit decisions to avoid asking.
codes.exclude_when: Receiving help that was not sought (e.g., an instructor's general announcement).

examples.quote: I finally went to office hours in week six and wished I'd gone in week one.
I didn't want to look stupid, so I never raised my hand.
examples.note: Deciding not to seek help still counts.

codes.name: AI tool use
codes.definition: Any description of using generative AI (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, etc.) for coursework, studying or research.
codes.include_when: How, when or why the participant uses AI tools, including attitudes about using them.
codes.exclude_when: General technology use with no AI component (e.g., Canvas, Zoom).

examples.quote: I'd paste the problem into ChatGPT and ask it to explain the first step only.

codes.name: Financial stress
codes.definition: Worry or constraints related to money that affect the participant's studies.
codes.include_when: Working to pay tuition, cost of books or housing, choosing fewer units for financial reasons.
codes.exclude_when: Neutral mentions of having a job with no stated pressure.

examples.quote: I was working thirty hours a week just to cover rent, so homework happened at 1am.

prompts.name: Interviewer turns
prompts.text: Do not code what the interviewer says; only code the participant's own statements. If a passage is an interviewer question, return no codes.

prompts.name: Be conservative
prompts.text: Prefer fewer, well-supported codes. Apply a code only when the passage itself shows it; do not infer from what the participant might mean.
